Securing NVIDIA’s EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying the standard security stack. These workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for the off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. We’re hiring an engineering leader to build and run Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters : the team responsible for implementing security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA’s hardware engineers design silicon on, spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud environments. You’ll operate as the peer counterpart to NVIDIA’s company-wide security organization and to hardware infrastructure engineering, translating enterprise security intent into controls that hold up at EDA scale without slowing chip design down.

Much of this is a build, not a maintain. You’ll have the authority to decide where standard tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and what NVIDIA engineers instead then lead a team to do it. If your depth is in large-scale networking and compute infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job and you’ve carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you are exactly who we want to talk to. We don’t expect you to arrive fluent in every security product category; we do expect you to own security outcomes from day one and to acquire the remaining domain breadth fast. Strong infrastructure mastery plus sharp security instincts beats a broad product résumé here. This is a role for someone who believes security engineering is engineering: automation, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.

What You’ll Be Doing:
- Build and lead the team. Grow and direct a team of engineers with a bias toward practical, production-proven results, and develop the leaders within it.  Own the technical roadmap. Partner with various other security teams and infrastructure engineering to architect the roadmap for EDA-specific security controls and ship them into production.
- Make the network and platform your control plane. Protection doesn’t depend just on what’s running inside the node.
- Engineer around hard constraints. Determine where conventional endpoint and workload security tooling fits, where it doesn’t, and design the alternative: security that protects multi-day compute jobs without degrading them.
- Make enforcement uniform. Drive consistent application of security frameworks across on-prem data centers and multi-cloud platforms where “consistent” means enforced, not documented.
- Run the full lifecycle of core infrastructure security technologies: selection, deployment, operation, and eventual replacement.

Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title and Summary

Senior Vice President, Software Engineering – Authentication

Overview

Lead one of Mastercard’s most strategically important global authentication engineering portfolios, advancing secure digital commerce, identity, biometrics, passkeys, and risk-based decisioning to enable trusted, low-friction payments.

Mastercard Authentication securely verifies card-not-present transactions through EMV 3DS solutions, including Identity Check, 3DS Server, and Access Control Server; risk-based authentication; Mastercard Passkeys; digital payment credentials for wallets; and in-store biometric checkout. These capabilities help customers improve approvals, reduce fraud, manage risk, and meet regulatory requirements.

The Senior Vice President, Software Engineering – Authentication has end-to-end accountability for engineering execution, resiliency, security, scalability, modernization, and operational performance. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, Digital Solutions, the role leads a global organization across the United States, India, and Europe and partners with Product, Architecture, Operations, Risk, and regional leadership.

Role

Engineering Leadership and Delivery

Lead the global engineering organization for Mastercard Authentication, spanning EMV 3DS, Risk based Authentication, Mastercard Passkeys and Digital Payment Credentials for Wallet based payments, and innovation for in-store biometric based checkout experiences.

Own end-to-end engineering delivery for authentication platforms with accountability for execution quality, availability, resiliency, scalability, latency, security, and operational performance.

Platform Strategy, Modernization, and Innovation

Set the long-term engineering strategy and modernization roadmap, including architectural convergence across the 3DS estate, cloud and distributed systems evolution, automation, reliability practices, and durable platform simplification.

Accelerate the shift from password and OTP-based authentication to biometric, passkey-based, and reusable authentication models that improve customer experience, increase approval rates, reduce cart abandonment and fraud , and support a more secure payments ecosystem.

Embed AI into the program’s engineering platforms, operating model, and software development lifecycle in alignment with Digital Payments priorities and responsible AI expectations for risk, bias, compliance, and data use.

Reporting directly to the Chief Technology and AI Officer, this role leads the teams and capabilities responsible for the core platform and ensures Judi is scalable, reliable, secure, performant, and built to support the company’s growth. The SVP will also lead the integration of artificial intelligence into the Judi platform and drive AI enablement across the Technology organization, using AI to improve engineering productivity, software quality, delivery velocity, and how technology teams build and operate the platform. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best-in-class.

As a Data Scientist Vice President within the Compliance, Conduct Operational Risk Data Analytics organization, you will be responsible for devising and developing Proofs of Concept (POCs) and deployable models using AI/ML techniques, algorithms and other statistical and numerical methods.  You will need to able to extract and work with large volumes of data (both structured and unstructured) from multiple sources, transforming it into an analysis-ready format to develop the data pipeline. Analyze complex/unstructured data to understand the business problem and use case

- 6+ years of related experience in Python, R or Scala with Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Physical Sciences, Econometrics, Statistics, or other any quantitative discipline.

roles.description:
About Invisible

Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most.

Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere.

Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets.

Profitable for more than half a decade, Invisible reached $134M in revenue and ranked as the number two fastest growing AI company on the 2024 Inc. 5000. In September 2025, we raised $100M in growth capital to accelerate our mission of making AI actually work in the enterprise and to advance our platform technology.

About the Role

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to set the technical strategy for Data Labs, the team that builds the benchmarking systems, data pipelines, and RL environments behind our AI training engagements. The frontier labs and enterprises we work with are changing how they train, evaluate, and deploy models every quarter. Your job is to see where that market is going and make sure Data Labs is built for it before our clients ask.

You'll decide which capabilities we invest in, which we standardize into platform, and which we leave to individual engagements. You'll track how training methods, evaluation practices, and data needs are shifting across the industry, and turn that into a technical roadmap and a point of view our commercial and research teams can sell against.

You'll lead a group of engineering managers, forward deployed engineers (FDEs), and senior ICs, and partner closely with applied research, product, and go-to-market leadership. This is a hands-on strategic role. You won't spend much time writing code, but you'll stay close enough to the technical work to make and defend hard architectural calls, and close enough to clients to know which calls matter.

What You'll Do

Technical Strategy & Roadmap
- Own the multi-year technical strategy for Data Labs, and translate it into a roadmap tied to where the AI training and evaluation market is heading.
- Decide where to build shared platform versus engagement-specific solutions, weighing reuse against team autonomy so platforms speed teams up rather than creating over-dependency.
- Set architectural direction for benchmarking infrastructure, data pipelines, and RL environments so they stay reproducible, portable across client deployments, and ready for the next generation of training methods.
- Anticipate technical shifts 6–18 months out, such as new post-training techniques, agentic evaluation, and synthetic data, and place the bets that keep Invisible ahead of them.

Director, Data Science - Consumer and Developer Experience (Remote-Eligible)

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description
At Capital One, we are relentless innovators with a proven track record of transforming customers’ experiences and the financial services industry. We’re delivering best-in-class innovation so that our more than 100 million customers can manage their finances with ease.

We consider ourselves the bank a technology company would build – empowered to use artificial intelligence (from machine learning to generative AI) to transform everyday banking into real-time, intelligent products that help customers improve their financial well-being. We’re all-in on the cloud and are a leader in the adoption of open source. We build our own products and release them with a speed and agility that allows us to get new customer experiences to market quickly. We’re going boldly where no bank has gone before. And, as a founder-led company, we are centered in our mission to help customers succeed.

The Role | General Responsibilities:

We’re seeking a Data Science Manager to support strategic priorities for Consumer and Developer Experience (CDX), as part of CDX’s product strategy team. CDX is an exciting space with diverse product responsibilities. The organization’s remit spans customer digital engagement, including the Capital One app; Capital One’s marketing platform, analytics, and personalization engine; the product suite used to manage all Capital One suppliers and vendors; products associated with the company’s risk management responsibilities; and more.

CDX’s product strategy team is a blend of strategy, product, and data science. We tackle the organization’s hardest strategic and analytical questions, delivering answers that fundamentally change the way we do business. We also act as an innovation lab, developing prototypes and partnering closely with product and engineering teams to translate conceptual visions into tangible, scaled digital experiences. We are looking for someone who thrives in this duality – someone who is equally energized by big-picture questions about where the world is going, thorny problems that require a strategic mindset and deep analytical rigor, and hands-on building.

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Senior Director, Quality Engineering – Performance, Scalability & Reliability

Location: San Francisco, CA | San Jose, CA

Team: Product & Engineering

Type: Full-Time

About Okta

Okta is the World’s Identity Company. We free everyone to safely use any technology—anywhere, on any device or app. Our Workforce and Customer Identity Clouds enable companies to protect the identities of their applicants, employees, and customers, while providing seamless access from any device, anywhere.

Thousands of customers, including Adobe, JetBlue, and Farmers Insurance, trust Okta to help them work faster, boost efficiency, and stay secure. Okta’s top priority is to provide a reliable, scalable, and secure platform. We are building a world where anyone can safely use any technology, and we need exceptional leaders to help us achieve this vision.

Position Overview

As the Senior Director of Performance, Scalability, and Reliability Engineering, you will be responsible for leading the global strategy, architecture, and execution of end-to-end performance testing, capacity planning, and system reliability across all Okta product lines.

In this high-impact executive role, you will lead a team of high-performing engineers and managers dedicated to ensuring the Okta Identity Cloud operates at peak efficiency, extreme throughput, and five-nines (99.999%) availability. You will partner closely with Core Engineering, Product Management, Infrastructure, and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) to drive proactive performance testing, push the limits of system scalability, and build guardrails that keep Okta resilient against massive enterprise loads. You will lead a team to conduct Integration testing and Perf testing across Okta Products and Platforms for Auth0 and Okta Workforce Identity suite of Products.

You will also lead scalability and reliability testing for Okta’s agentic AI products to ensure we can scale at Enterprise grade performance and deliver the same reliability as we do for SSO for global customers

What You’ll Do

Executive Leadership & Strategy: Define and execute the long-term technology roadmap for Integration testing, performance engineering, stress testing, scalability modeling, and reliability validation across Okta’s Workforce Identity Cloud and Customer Identity Cloud (Auth0).

Massive-Scale Performance & Chaos Testing : Oversee the development and maintenance of enterprise-scale load, stress, endurance, and chaos testing framework

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be a player-coach — someone who still ships code but also owns the engineering roadmap, team structure, and technical direction. You'll translate company strategy into engineering priorities, make sure the right things get built in the right order, and help a small, high-output team scale without losing speed.

You'll lead a small, technical engineering team that leverages AI to build the software infrastructure for running our automated lab. Your job is to make it the best small engineering team in biotech, and grow it thoughtfully as we scale.

This is not a management-track role where you stop building. You'll stay hands-on, especially as AI agents reshape what a small engineering team can accomplish. We expect you to be deeply technical, opinionated about architecture, and actively shipping — while also being the person who ensures the whole engineering org is pointed in the right direction and moving fast.

Day-to-day, that can mean:

 - Owning the engineering roadmap — deciding what to build, what to defer, and what to kill

 - Setting technical direction and architecture across frontend, backend, data pipelines, and lab-hardware integration

 - Shipping code yourself on the highest-leverage problems, not just reviewing it

 - Hiring, growing, and setting the bar for a team that ships fast and holds quality high — our lab runs on this software, so when things break, real experiments fail and real customers are affected

 - Building the team's AI-assisted development practices into a genuine speed advantage

The Director, Software Quality Engineering leads quality across our firmware, compiler, runtime, and inference-serving software. You will set the vision, define the test architecture, and lead both automation strategy and day-to-day execution for the Software Quality Engineering team.

Your first priority will be to assess our current processes, test content, tools, and frameworks. Create the practical roadmap while keeping current qualification work on schedule and developing the engineers who own it.

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Do you want to help the world build custom AI at scale? We’re hiring a founding Director to build and lead NVIDIA’s Forward Deployed Engineering organization for open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos, across North America. The mission is to turn open models into production-ready AI tuned to a specific domain, delivered through our partner ecosystem. We want any organization to build, own, and run its own AI on open source models, and this organization helps the ecosystem get there!

Unlike most forward deployed organizations, ours works primarily through NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem. Our FDEs work side by side with top partner engineering and research teams, co-lead joint customer engagements, and build the recipes and playbooks that help partners succeed and scale. This leader sets the strategy for North America, builds the organization, and carries the vision to partners, customers, and NVIDIA leadership. Are you an exceptional technical leader with deep roots in open model post-training and agent harness engineering, ready to build a world-class FDE organization? We’d love to meet you.

What you’ll be doing:
- This role sets the strategy and leads the team that delivers custom AI to end customers through NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem. The team deepens partner relationships and leads three-way engagements among NVIDIA, the partner, and the end customer. Our goal is hundreds of end customers running domain-specific Nemotron or Cosmos in production, supported by a strong ecosystem that delivers it.
- Hire and develop FDE leads, managers, and senior engineers across North America, and set a high bar for technical depth and customer impact. Create clear paths for growth and a team structure that scales with the ecosystem.
- The work stays technical. Set the technical direction for post-training, evaluation, harness engineering, and inference optimization, and be the person the team turns to on the hardest engagements. Keep up with the open model, post-training, and agents landscape, and bring new use cases and partner opportunities forward before partners ask.
- Partners are how we reach customers at scale. Build trusted relationships with leaders at partner and end-customer companies, shape joint plans and agreements, and see three-way engagements through to production. Set clear goals and track the results: partners adopting Nemotron, customers running in production, and customers willing to speak publicly. We help partners succeed on their own with reusable recipes, reference pipelines, and playbooks, so more developers can build domain-specific AI.

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

We’re looking for a seasoned engineering leader to own and scale the GPU and data center infrastructure that powers our neocloud platform. This hands-on leadership role sits at the intersection of software and hardware. You’ll lead the teams building validation platforms, lifecycle automation, and orchestration services that keep our fleet healthy, while also owning firmware qualification, hardware security, deployments, and data center operations across a fleet growing roughly 10x year over year. Our fleet runs under a 99.5% monthly availability SLA, so your reliability and automation work is directly tied to revenue.

You’ll set the technical charter for fleet reliability and operational excellence, defining north-star availability metrics and building automation that replaces today’s manual processes. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, Finance, and the executive team. The ideal candidate scales through systems rather than headcount, reasons from first principles, and leads from the front by digging into root causes. This is a full-time, senior leadership position.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Infrastructure Deployment & Fleet Management: Lead day-to-day fleet operations and greenfield deployments across co-location and owned facilities, from rack landing to customer availability. Own core fleet-health metrics and drive toward a 30-day time-to-sellable target.

 - Firmware Lifecycle Management: Build the pipeline to qualify and track every firmware release across 10+ SKUs and multiple OEMs/ODMs. Eliminate the qualification backlog (e.g., the ~66-day NVIDIA firmware lag), hold partners accountable, and evaluate in-house BMC development (OpenBMC).

 - Validation Framework & Platform: Consolidate siloed hardware automation pipelines and validation

### **Description**

BigHat Biosciences is seeking an exceptional player-coach to serve as Director of Machine Learning. Reporting to the CIO, you will own the technical direction, and a meaningful share of the hands-on execution, of BigHat's machine learning capabilities and the growing domain of machine learning operations, including agent development and how agents automate and extend our internally built computational platform and force multiply the impact of our teams.

We are looking for someone with genuine theoretical depth and the vision to say where ML-driven antibody design should go next. Your team will develop state-of-the-art antibody property models with the goal of iteratively improving our antibody designs and you’ll own the proof points that demonstrate the impact of these models. You’ll build agent services to bolster the agility and impact of our teams and work with frontier AI labs to adapt LLMs to new agentic antibody design challenges. As our platform value grows, so does our opportunity to create new and valuable platform partnerships. You will be accountable for the ML that differentiates our therapeutic programs, and for the modeling capabilities we put in front of data and model partners.

At BigHat, we only declare success upon synthesis of real antibodies with drug-like properties that improve patient outcomes. This is a rare opportunity to run frontier ML within a one-of-a-kind production platform, with an automated high-throughput wet lab generating the data to fuel it.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**ML strategy and vision:** Own and continuously sharpen BigHat's machine learning roadmap. Articulate where the field is going and where we intend to lead.

Develop and train models that support the safe and effective creation of increasingly sophisticated, multi-specific antibodies that patients need today.

**Frontier models joined with best-in-class data**: Apply frontier models, utilizing

BigHat’s unique datasets and data capabilities, against nature’s hardest protein design challenges. Optimize our design loop by integrating our lab, computational platform and data with LLM automation.

**Agentic direction**: Join forces across the CIO organization to steer our unified LLM and ML approach. Relentlessly drive our adoption of safe, impactful LLMs and similar models, agent frameworks and RL evaluation benchmarking frameworks to empower every BigHatter.

**Program impact:** Ensure that models, provenance, and benchmarks flow through our infrastructure without heroics, and that build-test-train design rounds fully leverage model insight for all 2k+ antibodies designed each week. roles.description:
Bring your expertise to JPMorgan Chase. As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorgan Chase strong and resilient. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best-in-class.
As a Third-Party Data Consumption Lead within Risk Management and Compliance, you will oversee all aspects of third-party data consumption, including credit bureau data, across all lines of business. You will implement robust controls, ensure regulatory alignment, and optimize data processes while collaborating with internal and external stakeholders.
You will play a pivotal role in managing third-party data consumption, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and optimizing data usage. You will engage with stakeholders to deliver technology and process enhancements, strengthen controls, and support audit readiness. This opportunity allows you to apply your technical and analytical skills in a collaborative environment, focusing on impactful initiatives that support our business and customers.
Job Responsibilities
- Manage processes, enhancements, and controls supporting consumer and business data consumption between Credit Reporting Agencies and Chase
- Collaborate with business partners and CRAs to ensure data requirements and application of Fair Credit Reporting Act standards
- Assess third-party data processes and gather user feedback to identify and implement enhancements
- Lead Agile transformation for third-party data, managing work across multiple JIRA boards and supporting sprint planning
- Support control framework and audit readiness through process updates, exception research, and evidence preparation
- Work with suppliers to standardize procedures for subscriber codes across all suppliers
- Analyze inventory data to identify opportunities for consolidating code usage across billing contacts and products
- Lead prioritization and implementation of analytical data request intakes
- Establish and strengthen controls around data transfers for security and efficiency
- Promote a fun, friendly, and inclusive team culture
- Engage with stakeholders to ensure project initiatives align with firm-wide guidelines

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
- Demonstrated leadership, organizational, and communication skills
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple complex initiatives
- Strong credit bureau knowledge
- Experience implementing projects in an Agile environment
- Proficiency in Microsoft Project, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and strong written and verbal communication skills
- Working knowledge of Agile methodologies and JIRA board management
- Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of relevant work experience
